The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl isatin, which I read as follows.

**Left biaryl part.** The top ring carries CO2H at the meta position relative to the biaryl bond. The second ring is attached to the first at one carbon. Its adjacent carbon bears OH, and the next carbon after that bears the NH–N= group. So the substituents are ring-attached, then OH, then NH, in consecutive positions.

**Hydrazone linker.** The NH is bonded to an N that is double-bonded to C3 of the indolinone.

**Indolinone part.** C3 is attached to C2 (C=O), which is attached to N1. N1 carries a 3-methylphenyl group and is also bonded to the benzo ring.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with a defined geometry. The NH sits on the lower left of the N, and the indole's C3 sits to the lower right. At C3, the carbonyl C2 lies to the left and the aromatic C3a to the right. Taking the N=C bond, the NH substituent on N points up-left, toward the left side of the molecule. On C3, the C2 (carbonyl) is on the left and below. So NH and C2 are on the same side, which is Z with respect to C2. In SMILES this is written as `N/N=C1/C(=O)...` with the appropriate arrangement.

Writing the SMILES: `OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3cccc(C)c3)c3ccccc23)c1O`

Checking the geometry: the fragment `N/N=C2\C(=O)` means the N's preceding atom is "below" the N=C bond, and C(=O) after C2 with `\` is "below" the C. Both are on the same side, so NH and C2 are cis, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3cccc(C)c3)c3ccccc23)c1O
